outcome: maternal complications (infection, fever, wound dehiscence, bleeding, organ damage, anemia, respiratory tract infection, postpartum cardiomyopathy)
cohort: The study included 200 pregnant subjects (mean age 31.5 years, mean BMI 26.8 kg/m2, majority from rural residence) who underwent cesarean section.
finding: Maternal complications were encountered in 31% of subjects undergoing cesarean section.
mod_finding: Postoperative complications, particularly surgical site infection, were identified as the most common type of maternal complications associated with cesarean section.
birth_weight: greater than or equal to 1000 g
gest_age: greater than or equal to 28 weeks
